primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Oxidation of heme iron from the ferrous (Fe2+) to ferric (Fe3+) state creates methemoglobin. Ferric heme cannot bind oxygen and also increases oxygen affinity at remaining ferrous heme sites, impairing tissue oxygen unloading.
vignette: During recovery from an uncomplicated outpatient procedure, a 29-year-old patient develops headache, dyspnea, and cyanosis. Supplemental oxygen produces little change in the pulse oximetry reading. Arterial blood gas analysis shows a normal PaO2, and the drawn blood is chocolate-brown. Co-oximetry demonstrates an increased methemoglobin fraction.
lead: Which molecular change in hemoglobin most directly explains this patient's impaired oxygen delivery?
correct: Oxidation of heme iron from Fe2+ to Fe3+
distractors: Formation of carboxyhemoglobin by carbon monoxide binding to hemoglobin
Impaired heme synthesis caused by lead-mediated enzyme inhibition
distractor_notes: Carbon monoxide forms carboxyhemoglobin and impairs oxygen delivery, but standard pulse oximetry cannot reliably distinguish carboxyhemoglobin from oxyhemoglobin; the stem instead directly identifies increased methemoglobin.
Hemoglobin S polymerizes in the deoxygenated state and causes sickling, hemolysis, and vaso-occlusion; it does not create a methemoglobin fraction.
Beta-thalassemia is a quantitative defect with reduced or absent beta-globin synthesis, producing chronic anemia rather than oxidation of heme iron.
Lead interferes with enzymes involved in heme synthesis and can cause anemia; it does not convert hemoglobin iron to the ferric methemoglobin state.
key_expl: The combination of cyanosis that responds poorly to supplemental oxygen, a normal arterial PaO2, chocolate-brown blood, and an increased methemoglobin fraction identifies methemoglobinemia. In methemoglobin, heme iron is oxidized from Fe2+ to Fe3+. Ferric heme cannot bind oxygen, and its presence also increases oxygen affinity at the remaining Fe2+ sites, further limiting oxygen release to tissues.
objective: Recognize methemoglobinemia from a dyshemoglobinemia pattern and link it to oxidation of heme iron from Fe2+ to Fe3+, which prevents oxygen binding and impairs tissue oxygen delivery.
clues: cyanosis poorly responsive to supplemental oxygen
normal PaO2 despite abnormal pulse oximetry

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Methemoglobinemia
sources.support: NCBI states that methemoglobinemia results from oxidation of heme iron from Fe2+ to Fe3+; ferric heme cannot bind oxygen and shifts remaining hemoglobin toward higher oxygen affinity. It also identifies refractory cyanosis, chocolate-brown blood, a saturation gap/normal blood-gas oxygen calculation pattern, and co-oximetry as diagnostic features.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
sources.support: NCBI states that carbon monoxide forms carboxyhemoglobin, reduces oxygen-carrying capacity, left-shifts oxygen unloading, and can preserve measured blood PaO2; standard pulse oximetry cannot reliably identify carboxyhemoglobin. The differential section contrasts this with methemoglobinemia.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Sickle Cell Anemia
sources.support: NCBI states that deoxygenated hemoglobin S forms rigid polymers that drive erythrocyte sickling, hemolysis, and vaso-occlusive disease.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Beta Thalassemia
sources.support: NCBI describes beta-thalassemia as a quantitative hemoglobin synthesis disorder caused by reduced or absent beta-globin production.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Lead Toxicity
sources.support: NCBI states that lead causes anemia by interfering with enzymes involved in heme synthesis and by damaging erythrocyte integrity.
